lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: comparing functions across algebraic, graphical, numerical, and verbal forms
lessonRef.title: Performance task build: comparing functions across algebraic, graphical, numerical, and verbal forms

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: The function f(x) = 2(x − 2)² − 1 opens upward. State its minimum value and where it occurs.
A polynomial has degree 2 and leading coefficient 3. Describe its end behaviour.
choices: the left end falls and the right end rises
the left end rises and the right end falls

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: For f(x) = (x + 3) / (x + 1), state the vertical asymptote and the horizontal asymptote.
Function f is given in vertex form as f(x) = −(x + 2)² − 7, so it opens downward. Function g is given by a table whose greatest output is -2. Which function has the greater maximum, and by how much?
The function f(x) = 4(x + 3)² − 12 opens upward. State its minimum value and where it occurs.
A polynomial has degree 4 and leading coefficient 5. Describe its end behaviour.
choices: the left end falls and the right end rises
the left end rises and the right end falls

items.prompt: For f(x) = (x + 1) / (x + 2), state the vertical asymptote and the horizontal asymptote.
Function f is given in vertex form as f(x) = −(x − 6)² + 3, so it opens downward. Function g is given by a table whose greatest output is 8. Which function has the greater maximum, and by how much?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Carry the build to a result and state the check that would catch an error in it.

items.prompt: The function f(x) = 3(x − 3)² − 9 opens upward. State its minimum value and where it occurs.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A polynomial has degree 4 and leading coefficient -3. Describe its end behaviour.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
